title: SoK: Attack and Defense Landscape of Agentic AI Systems
pdf_path: papers/SoK_Attack and Defense Landscape of Agentic AI Systems.pdf
threat_model_summary: Three adversary classes: external (controls retrieved content; V1 indirect prompt injection, V2 malicious data, V3 tool poisoning), user-level (V4 direct prompt injection), internal (V5 model poisoning, V6 memory poisoning).
core_contributions: First system-wide SoK of agent security
Seven design dimensions
Six attack vectors and seven risk categories
Four-layer defense landscape
Open challenges
limitations: No formal definitions or proofs
Subjective literature selection
Taxonomy categories overlap
Limited coverage of side channels and real deployments
theoretical_crypto_links: No formal cryptographic model; IAM/delegation/audit described only as system principles
Contextual security is a policy/semantic goal, not a cryptographic game
applied_crypto_links: OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect delegation
ETDI signed and versioned tool definitions
Encrypted credential storage and TEE
Short-lived tokens and revocation

title: Position: AI Agents Need Authenticated Delegation
pdf_path: papers/Position_AI Agents Need Authenticated Delegation.pdf
threat_model_summary: Implicit adversary model centered on token threats: tampering, ID spoofing, instance spoofing, identity correlation, session hijacking, endpoint impersonation, scope abuse and cross-instance privilege escalation (Appendix B.5).
core_contributions: Argues authenticated delegation is critical for agents
Extends OIDC/OAuth 2.0 with user ID-token, Agent-ID token and user-signed delegation token
Proposes structured resource scoping plus natural-language translation and human review
Legal and governance analysis
limitations: No formal security definition or proof
No implementation or experiments
OIDC privacy centralization and sign-in overhead
Natural-language policy translation unreliable
Revocation consistency and key compromise unaddressed
theoretical_crypto_links: Delegation credential unforgeability and scope non-amplification are natural formal targets (our inference, not paper's)
Signatures, commitments, anonymous credentials and ZK are plausible tools (inference)
applied_crypto_links: User-signed delegation token with expiry and revocation endpoint
W3C VC selective disclosure
OIDC pairwise pseudonyms, audience restriction, dynamic client registration
Cross-domain OP federation for agent mutual authentication

title: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion
pdf_path: papers/FragFuse_Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion.pdf
threat_model_summary: Ordinary black-box user; knows public access-control policy and that retrieval is similarity-based; cannot access memory bank or AC internals; can observe accept/reject and interact over multiple turns.
core_contributions: First memory-based temporal-channel attack bypassing agent access control
Three-stage black-box pipeline (fragment discovery, carrier injection, retrieval/fusion)
Offline surrogate constrained optimization of fusion instruction
Evaluation across four agents, three AC mechanisms and three LLMs
limitations: Access control checks only current query by design
Requires persistent memory and multiple interactions
Task-domain generalization unproven
Weak against post-hoc action inspection
Fusion depends on capable backbone LLM
theoretical_crypto_links: No cryptographic construction
Motivates history-dependent authorization soundness as a formal property (our inference)
applied_crypto_links: Memory write provenance/authentication and encrypted memory are plausible mitigations (our inference, not evaluated)
Retrieval-time policy enforcement after memory augmentation (system, not crypto)

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
pdf_path: papers/SAGA_A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems.pdf

Implementation and multi-region performance evaluation, plus RAFT replication and AWS scaling

Self-replicating agents and credential sharing (C3/C4) remain out of scope
Malicious Provider only mitigated by replication/audit, not formally modeled
Authorization policy is enforced by a trusted Provider; policy correctness is not cryptographic
Requires globally routable IPs; no NAT traversal
theoretical_crypto_links: Symbolic Dolev-Yao model and ProVerif proofs of authentication/secrecy
X25519 Diffie-Hellman, one-time keys, access-control tokens, X.509 identity
